messages:
maya: Quick question — thinking through SLO-driven routing + model-variant fallback. Want a pattern where each customer tier and region declares a latency SLO and an availability cb threshold, and we automatically route + fallback to compatible variants when CB trips. Thoughts?
kevin: short answer: yes. longer: need a clear policy DSL + strong telemetry. otherwise matchmaking gets messy across quantized vs full fp16 variants. :+1:
li: telemetry is key. we need per-(route,model,region,tier) metrics: p50/p95 latency, errors, cb_open_count, fallback_rate. those should feed the console.
sarah: UX thought — surface suggested defaults per tier (startup, standard, enterprise) but allow per-customer overrides behind a feature flag. show expected cost delta when fallback happens.
dmitri: compatibility matrix is annoying. we should only allow fallbacks that preserve interface (same tokenizer, same output schema). create a model-compatibility tag set to filter.
maya: agree on compatibility. Also thinking of cb thresholds being % of failing requests in window vs median latency miss rate. Which do we want?
kevin: both. primary CB on availability/errors (5xx rate), secondary soft-gating on latency (if p95 > SLO for X windows, start routing to lower-latency variant).
li: proposal: circuit_breaker: type: "error_rate" window_s: 60 threshold_pct: 5 action: open_and_route_fallback
kevin: + add hysteresis: min_open_seconds and cooldown. otherwise flip-flopping.
sarah: console flow: a slider for latency SLO (ms) + a small numeric for cb_threshold_pct, and a checkbox for "allow model fallback". show simulated impact using historic telemetry.
maya: throwing a rough DSL sketch here:
```
policy {
  route: "/v1/generate"
  tiers {
    default {
      latency_slo_ms: 200
      cb_error_pct: 10
      fallback_allowed: true
      fallback_priority: ["gptq-4-8k","llama-q2a"]
    }
    enterprise {
      latency_slo_ms: 100
      cb_error_pct: 3
      fallback_allowed: false
    }
  }
}
```
kevin: nice. also allow regional overrides: "eu": { … } so legal/regional capacity differences handled.
dmitri: add model-signature check before routing to fallback: if model.sig != request.expected_sig -> reject or transform. we can't silently change schema.
li: ops note: telemetry labels should include policy_id and decision_reason (e.g., cb_open, route_ok, fallback_for_latency). that'll help debugging.
sarah: rollout UX: new policy default to "staging" then can be promoted. provide a canary checkbox: "start with N% traffic" and automatic rollback if key metrics degrade.
maya: how about automated tuning: console can recommend cb thresholds based on observed error distribution and latency SLO — suggest a conservative default and show risk bars.
kevin: implementation-wise: routing layer keeps a fast in-memory circuit state per (policy,region,tier). updates from streaming telemetry (prometheus counters or kafka). on CB open, we mark route decisions and emit event.
routing-bot: policy-deploy: staging policy "sla-gating/2026-03-18-1" applied to staging cluster. :rocket:
dmitri: question: do we allow tiered fallbacks where request can hop more than once (enterprise->team->default)? that could hide issues.
li: allow a max_fallback_depth param. default 1.
sarah: also need an audit trail for fallback decisions (who configured, when, why) — compliance asks.
maya: ok action items: 1) kevin + dmitri: draft compatibility check API (model.sig + tokenizer). 2) li: inventory telemetry labels + alerts for CB. 3) sarah + maya: mock console screens with simulated cost impact. 4) kevin: prototype in-memory cb state and hysteresis.
kevin: I'll start a RFC branch and a tiny prototype. timeline?
maya: aim for RFC end of next week. prototyping over next sprint.
dmitri: I'll add tests for signature/format compatibility.
li: I'll sketch queries and alert rules.
sarah: will mock screens by Friday.
maya: cool — thanks all. If anyone wants to pair on the DSL + UX tradeoffs ping me. :eyes:
